evidence_boundary: Calculated and structural statements about a supplied model. They do not establish that the model describes a physical system, and they do not establish novelty; both need comparison with experiment and with the literature.
question: Does raising the barrier of the rf-SQUID annealer (beta through 1) write the persistent-current state chosen by a weak flux bias, and with which law?
assumptions: phase relative to half flux, theta = phi - pi; time in units of 1/omega_LC; damping 1/Q = 0.5 (the census gives no Q; annealer qubits are treated as a damped classical latch)
beta = beta_eff set by the CCJJ flux (census: beta_eff ~ 2.43 at full anneal)
noise D = gam kT/U_q with T = 53 mK and U_q/k_B ~ 30 K (L_q = 265 pH): D ~ 9e-4
inductive coupling as J theta_i theta_j (mean-field flux coupling); J > 0 antiferromagnetic

B 81, 134510 (2010), arXiv:0909.4321 (full text); Harris, R. et al., 'Experimental investigation of an eight-qubit unit cell in a superconducting optimization processor', Phys. Rev. Phys. 83, 054401 (2020), arXiv:1903.06559 (full text); Kjaergaard, M., Schwartz, M. E., Braumueller, J., Krantz, P., Wang, J. I.-J., Gustavsson, S., Oliver, W. D., 'Superconducting qubits: current state of play', Annu. Rev. Condens. Matter Phys. 11, 369 (2020), arXiv:1905.13641 (full text)
